Review the uncommitted working-tree change (git diff plus untracked files; use `git status --short` and `git diff` in /home/ubuntu/.t3/worktrees/surveybeat-next/t3-ae08fbf6-1c2adf97687a0134) for GitHub issue 308 of the SurveyBeat app: "offboard an Organization". Read-only review; do not edit files, do not run git commit/checkout/config. Do not run the slow full test suites; reading code and running single test files is fine.

Locked design to check the code against (report deviations, not alternative designs):
- ADR docs/adr/0028-offboarding-returns-no-results.md (new). ADR 0003 stands: the export must contain only Organization id/name/min group size/AI flag/default locale; Teams (id,name,time zone); People (id,email,organizationAdmin,locale,time zone,removedAt,erasedAt); Memberships incl. ended; Pulses and their Questions. It must contain NO Result, comment, theme, Action, Note, Submission, Answer, participation, Invitation token, token hash, Edit key, email body, auth user id, or session.
- New permission organization.offboard granted only to admin (packages/domain/src/people/Permissions.ts). Export and delete both use it; Lead/member get 403; the caller's own Person is no substitute.
- POST /api/organization/offboarding {confirmation} must equal the Organization's stored name exactly; wrong name -> existing ErasureNotConfirmed 422 and changes nothing; same-origin required. GET /api/organization/offboarding-export admin only. Both classified NoResultData in packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts.
- Durable Object wipe (packages/cloudflare/src/organization/Offboarding.ts wipeOrganization, wired in Organization.ts): deleteAlarm() then deleteAll(), nothing after, safe when empty.
- Crash order, implemented in packages/domain/src/people/DirectoryFlow.ts offboardOrganization + packages/cloudflare/src/auth/D1OrganizationOffboarding.ts + migration packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0012_organization_offboarding.sql (+ lock): (1) resolve session/Organization like currentMember; (2) DO still has the Person as admin -> require typed name, insert organization_offboarding row for the auth user id, an existing row must be the same auth user id; (3) DO no longer has the Person -> continue only if organization_offboarding.actor_user_id is the session user, name not asked again; (4) anyone else Forbidden, wrong name writes no row and deletes nothing; (5) delete this Organization's D1 invitation_index, test_invitation_index, test_submission_index, submission_index, auth_session_organization; (6) DO wipe; (7) read person_index.auth_user_id for the Organization BEFORE deleting, delete captured_email by message_id from this Organization's email_message rows (NEVER by recipient), then email_message, then person_index, organization_claim, organization_offboarding, organization_index for this Organization; (8) for each collected auth user id call the existing PeopleIndex.eraseAccount (keeps the account when any person_index row remains, including removed_at set). Must not delete auth_organization/auth_member/auth_invitation. Another Organization's rows and DO untouched. Not LastAdmin, not LastLead.
- UI (apps/web): danger zone on the Organization settings screen; download first, then type Organization name; says deletion cannot be undone and backups expire after Policy.backupRetentionDays; no new field in the settings response; all text from apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts. apps/web/src/messages/legalPrivacy.ts and legalAgreements.ts must be unchanged. No existing e2e spec weakened (infra/tests/e2e).
- Tests: packages/cloudflare/src/OrganizationOffboarding.privacy.test.ts (real migrations over node sqlite), DirectoryApi.test.ts additions, packages/domain/src/people/Offboarding.test.ts, web scene/story tests. Check they would really fail if the guarantee broke.
- Glossary terms: Pulse, Person, Round, Submission, Answer, Invitation, Organization, Team, Lead; never User/Response/Respondent in new user-facing text or docs.
- Repo rules (AGENTS.md): no `any`/`as` assertions outside *.test.ts, no prose comments in non-test code, explicit .ts import extensions, no edit to an already-merged migration.

Report concrete defects only (file:line, what breaks, how), ranked by severity, plus anything in the list above that is missing. Say explicitly if you find nothing in a category. Keep the report under 60 lines.

I'm going through the test results and export logic now. The after-crash test passes with an empty name, and the export and pulse settings look fine. I'm also noting a possible gap: the Durable Object wipe was only checked through storage, not against a real DO, and I'm looking at the in-memory side too.

I'm checking whether the wipe could leave the in-memory Durable Object broken: after deleteAll the SQLite tables are gone, so any query on that same instance would fail with "no such table." If a retry hits the cached instance, the linked-person lookup could die with a 500 instead of returning nothing. It seems plausible but I'm not sure whether the instance gets evicted first.

Now I'm checking the retry path after a crash: a fresh Durable Object runs its migrations again and starts with empty tables, so the active-person lookup should just return none. The session-cookie lookup should also come back empty without error. The `onSome` branch and the non-admin Forbidden rejection look correct, and I'm still looking at whether eraseAccount revokes the session cookie.

content.text:
**Verdict: no BLOCKER or MAJOR defects found.** The implementation matches the locked design. I ran `OrganizationOffboarding.privacy.test.ts` (14 tests, in the privacy project), `Offboarding.test.ts` and `Permissions.test.ts`. They all pass. I did not run the web scene/story tests or the typecheck and lint.

**Matches the design**
- **Permission:** `organization.offboard` is granted only to `admin` (`Permissions.ts`).
  - Export and delete both go through `offboardingAccess`.
  - A Lead or member gets Forbidden, and `begin` is never reached.
- **Confirmation:** `offboardingConfirmation` compares the typed name to `state.organizationName` with strict `!==`. A wrong name returns `ErasureNotConfirmed` (422) before any D1 write.
- **Same origin:** both routes call `requireSameOrigin` first. `PrivacyRegistry.ts` classifies both as `NoResultData`.
- **Crash order** in `DirectoryFlow.ts` `offboardOrganization`:
  - With a Member, it checks the name, then `begin`. An existing row for another account gives Forbidden.
  - With no Member, it continues only if `pending(userId)` finds a row, and does not ask for the name again. Otherwise it is Forbidden.
  - Then `revokeAccess`, then `wipe`, then `removeIndex`, then `eraseAccount` per collected account.
- **`D1OrganizationOffboarding.ts`:**
  - `revokeAccess` deletes exactly the 4 token indexes plus `auth_session_organization`, each by `organization_id`.
  - `removeIndex` reads `person_index.auth_user_id` before deleting.
  - It deletes `captured_email` by `message_id` subselect on `email_message`, never by recipient. A privacy test keeps the `captured-sign-in` row to prove this.
  - It deletes `email_message`, `person_index`, `organization_claim`, `organization_offboarding` and `organization_index`.
  - It does not touch `auth_organization`, `auth_member` or `auth_invitation`.
- **DO wipe:** `wipeOrganization` is `deleteAlarm()` then `deleteAll()` and nothing after. It is wired in `Organization.ts` and `MainWorker.ts`.
- **Migration:** `0012` is new, and its SHA is in `d1-migrations.lock.json`. No merged migration was edited.
- **Export contents:** `offboardingExportOf` emits only the allowed fields.
  - It has no auth user id, tokens, Results, Answers or Notes.
  - The privacy test seeds marker strings for each forbidden item and asserts none appear.
- **UI:**
  - The danger zone shows download first, then a name field.
  - It says deletion cannot be undone, and the backup days come from `Policy.backupRetentionDays`.
  - Text is in `catalog.ts`.
  - No settings-response field was added.
  - `legalPrivacy.ts` and `legalAgreements.ts` are unchanged, and `infra/` has no diff.
- **Tests:**
  - `OrganizationOffboarding.privacy.test.ts` runs on real migrations over node sqlite.
  - Its tests would fail if a delete were dropped, if deletion were by recipient, if the other Organization were touched, or if the account were erased despite a remaining (including removed) Person.

**Findings (all MINOR)**

1. `packages/cloudflare/src/auth/D1OrganizationOffboarding.ts` (`removeIndex`) can leak an auth account on retry. `person_index` is deleted before `organization_offboarding` and `organization_index`, and the statements are not batched.
   - If the Worker stops after the `person_index` delete, the offboarding row remains and the same admin can retry.
   - The retry reads zero auth user ids, so `eraseAccount` is never called for accounts that only belonged here.
   - ADR 0028 acknowledges the 7-to-8 window but not this one.
   - Fix: delete `organization_offboarding` and `organization_index` before `person_index`, or issue the deletes as one D1 `batch`. A crash would then leave either everything or nothing of the index.

2. `packages/domain/src/people/DirectoryFlow.ts` (`offboardOrganization`, `onSome` branch) strands a pending offboarding in one case. If the admin has a pending row for Organization A but the session resolves to a Member of Organization B, the code takes the Member branch and never consults `pending`. Organization A can then only be finished after the session no longer resolves to B. This is an edge case. A fix would be to prefer `pending(userId)` when it names an Organization other than `member.organization.id`.

3. `apps/web/src/app/directory.ts` (`dangerZoneView`) marks the copy as downloaded on a click of the `<a download>` link, not on a successful download. A failed GET (403, network error) still unlocks the delete control. This is only a UI nudge, because the server enforces nothing about it. It is acceptable, but worth knowing that "download first" is advisory.

4. `packages/cloudflare/src/DirectoryApi.test.ts` (export test) asserts `not.toMatch(/result|submission|answer|token/i)` on the body. That is a weak check. The strong marker-based check is in the privacy test, so this is not blocking.

5. Style: `packages/cloudflare/src/OrganizationOffboarding.privacy.test.ts` uses `as unknown as` casts, which is allowed in `*.test.ts`. The prose comment in `Offboarding.ts` (the JSDoc above `OrganizationOffboardingExport` and the `OrganizationOffboardingShape` member docs) conflicts with the `no-comments/no-comments` rule, which runs at `error` for non-test code. `pnpm lint` will probably flag these. I did not run lint. If it does, move the reason into the ADR and names.

**Missing from your list**
- Nothing required is missing.
- No new web scene/story assertions for the wrong-name 422 path were checked in depth.
- I did not run the e2e specs. `infra/` is unchanged, so none are weakened.
